notes: Each case starts on a fresh fake SEI server (these commands use no database), applies its setup calls in order, and runs the command with exactly the recorded environment, nothing inherited; <SEI_URL> stands for the fake's base URL.

cases.name: test-login lists every configuration problem
cases.stderr:
error: invalid configuration:
  - SEI_URL is required (the SEI address, e.g. https://sei.rr.gov.br)
  - SEI_USERNAME is required
  - SEI_PASSWORD is required (or SEI_PASSWORD_FILE, or SEI_PASSWORD_CMD)
  - SEI_ORG is required (acronym or numeric id; the orgs subcommand lists them)

interrupt.note: Go ran the command with a context cancelled before it started. The configuration is valid, so it is read; the first request to SEI then fails with the cancellation. A replay sends SIGINT after the process has started and before the fake SEI answers its first request (hold that answer until the signal is delivered). test-login prints nothing before every call has returned, so stdout is empty for any interrupt that lands before the last answer.
